**Fairfax, VA – November 13, 2025 –**[WidePoint Corporation](https://www.widepoint.com/) **(NYSE American:**[WYY](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/WYY?p=WYY) **)** , a federally certified provider of Trusted Mobility Management (TM2) solutions, reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2025.


---


**Fairfax, VA – November 12, 2026 –**[WidePoint Corporation](https://www.widepoint.com/) **(NYSE American:**[WYY](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/WYY?p=WYY) **)** , a leading provider of Secure Mobility Management solutions, reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.


#####


**Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Operational Highlights:**


- 37


th


consecutive quarter of positive Adjusted EBITDA


- 12


th


consecutive quarter of positive free cash flow


- Awarded 40 new and replacement task orders with a total value of approximately $33.7 million during the third quarter under the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s (“DHS”) Cellular Wireless Managed Services (“CWMS”) 2.5 bridge contract


- Awarded the CWMS 2.5 bridge contract, a 6-month IDIQ with a ceiling value of approximately $113 million


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights:**


- Revenues were $45.1 million, an increase of $9.5 million from the same quarter last year


- Gross margin was 14%, and gross margin excluding carrier services revenue was 30%


- Net loss was $(192,000) or $(0.02) per share, compared to a net loss of $(559,000) or a loss of $(0.06) per share in the same quarter last year


- Adjusted EBITDA


1 , a non-GAAP financial measure, was $338,000 compared to $344,000 in the same quarter last year


- Free cash flow


1 , a non-GAAP financial measure, was $338,000 compared to $324,000 in the same quarter last year


- As of September 30, 2026, unrestricted cash was $10.1 million with no bank debt


- As of September 30, 2026, federal contract backlog was approximately $209 million


**Nine Months 2026 Financial Highlights:**


- Revenues were $123.6 million, an increase of $17.3 million from the same period last year


- Gross margin was 14%, and gross margin excluding carrier services revenue was 33%


- Net loss was $(49,000) or $(0.00) per share, compared to a net loss of $(1.9) million or a loss of $(0.20) per share in the same period last year


- Adjusted EBITDA


1 , a non-GAAP financial measure, was $1.7 million, a 178% increase from the same period last year


- Free cash flow


1 , a non-GAAP financial measure, was $1.6 million, a 242% increase from the same period last year

**Management Commentary**


WidePoint CEO, Jin Kang commented: “The decision by the Government Accountability Office (“GAO”) to sustain the protest related to the CWMS 3.0 award has undoubtedly created near-term disruption; however, we believe the issues are temporary in nature. While sustained protests are not unprecedented in federal procurement, we recognize this was an unexpected setback.


With respect to the pending CWMS 3.0 procurement, DHS has requested revised proposals, and WidePoint has submitted a revised proposal for evaluation by DHS. We await DHS’s announcement of the results of its evaluation and the resulting award decision. We will have no further comment on the status of the CWMS 3.0 procurement at this time.


“Importantly, operations continue uninterrupted under the CWMS 2.5 bridge contract. In the third quarter alone, we received 40 new and replacement task orders valued at approximately $33.7 million and we continue to receive additional task orders in the fourth quarter. We also hold CWMS 2.0 task orders extending into 2027, providing a meaningful runway as the CWMS 3.0 award process moves towards resolution.


“Beyond CWMS, integration efforts under the ATV contract continue to advance, and we remain on track for our targeted year-end go-live. We also recently received a letter of authorization from CDW as we work toward potentially becoming the official subcontractor supporting CDW’s role as the Official IT Equipment and Solutions Provider for the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games and Team USA. In addition, we strengthened our federal growth initiative through the hiring a professional with extensive experience in federal government acquisitions, IDIQ contracts, and the implementation of a Program Management Office (PMO) model similar to that of the DHS PMO model to maximize opportunities under the NASA SEWP VI contract vehicle. Together, these developments reinforce our confidence in WidePoint’s long-term growth prospects and execution against multiple strategic opportunities.”

##### **About WidePoint**


WidePoint Corporation (NYSE American: WYY) is a leading technology Managed Solution Provider (MSP) dedicated to securing and protecting the mobile workforce and enterprise landscape. ##### **Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


WidePoint uses a variety of operational and financial metrics, including non-GAAP financial measures such as EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, and Free cashflow, to enable it to analyze its performance and financial condition. The presentation of non-GAAP financial information should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of GAAP Net income to EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA and Free cashflow is provided below:


[View Full Size](https://www.widepoint.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/3b.png)


WidePoint uses EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Free cashflow as supplemental non-GAAP measure of performance. WidePoint defines EBITDA as net income excluding (i) interest expense, (ii) provision for or benefit from income taxes, (iii) depreciation and amortization, and (iv) Impairment charges. Adjusted EBITDA excludes certain amounts included in EBITDA such as stock-based compensation expense. WidePoint defined Free cashflow as Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures. Management believes that adjustments for certain non-cash or other items and the exclusion of certain pass-through revenue and expenses should enhance stockholders’ ability to evaluate the Company’s performance, as such measures provide additional insights into the factors and trends affecting its business. Therefore, the Company excludes these items from its GAAP financial measures to calculate these unaudited non-GAAP measures. These unaudited non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies and should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for GAAP.
